standard_prerequisites.name: A module is finite projective if and only if it is finitely presented and flat
standard_prerequisites.source_reference: Algebra, Lemma \ref{algebra-lemma-finite-projective}, cited at proof lines 903-904
standard_prerequisites.use: Reduces the equivalence to matching finite presentation and flatness.

standard_prerequisites.name: Flatness and finiteness of the module associated to a triple over the fibre product
standard_prerequisites.source_reference: Lemmas \ref{lemma-flat-module-over-fibre-product} and \ref{lemma-finite-module-over-fibre-product}, cited at proof lines 905-907 and again at 914 and 929
standard_prerequisites.use: Reduce to finite presentability of the fibre product module and provide the finiteness input for the kernel.

standard_prerequisites.name: The kernel of a surjection from a finite free module onto a finite module is finite
standard_prerequisites.source_reference: Algebra, Lemma \ref{algebra-lemma-extension}, cited at proof lines 927-928
standard_prerequisites.use: Shows that the kernels after base change are finite modules.

standard_prerequisites.name: Flatness makes the tensor product of a short exact sequence with a module exact
standard_prerequisites.source_reference: Algebra, Lemma \ref{algebra-lemma-flat-tor-zero}, cited at proof lines 936-938
standard_prerequisites.use: Gives the identifications K_B tensor A = K_A = K_{A'} tensor A that the finiteness criterion needs.

core_obligations: Reduce finite projectivity to finite presentation plus flatness and invoke the flatness result for triples (proof lines 903-907).
Choose a surjection from a finite free module onto the fibre product module and define its kernel (proof lines 914-916).
Base change the surjection along the two ring maps and record the kernels on the two sides (proof lines 917-921).
Show that the canonical map from the kernel to the fibre product of the two kernels is an isomorphism (proof lines 922-926).
Verify the two kernel identifications using flatness, and conclude that the kernel is finite, hence that the module is finitely presented (proof lines 927-940).
proof_roadmap: Reduce to finite presentation of the fibre product module (proof lines 903-907).
Compare kernels after choosing a free presentation (proof lines 914-926).
Use flatness to identify the kernels and finish (proof lines 927-940).
difficulty_reason: The lemma identifies the category of finite projective modules over the fibre product of two rings with the category of triples of a finite projective module over one factor, a finite projective module over the other, and an isomorphism after base change. The proof reduces finite projectivity to finite presentation plus flatness, uses the earlier flatness and finiteness results to reduce to showing that the fibre product module is finitely presented, then chooses a surjection from a finite free module, compares the kernel with the fibre product of the kernels obtained after base change, verifies that the comparison map is an isomorphism, and concludes finite generation of the kernel from the exactness of the two sequences after tensoring, which is exactly where flatness of the two given modules is used.
